utterances.text: What is related in the article is the talk that I had with the man. Of course now I do not remember the exact details of the conversation I had with him. What there is in the article is what was said between me and him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This man, as far as you could see, did not exhibit any consequences of torture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That man was not tortured in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No person was tortured before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Harraz, I should like to ask you several questions related to your article of July 25th . So you were given authorisation to visit the frontline, the line of separation with the Serbs; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was a confrontation site with the Serbs, but the area I visited was a mountainous area and there was an exchange of fire between the two parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can testify that around 2.00, through a very bad and dangerous road, you climbed up high into the mountains, up to the first command post of the artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you recall your article, after these two hours of a ride that was really dangerous, you arrived at the command post of the Bosnian artillery, where you saw, as means of combat of the Territorial Defence of Konjic, a cannon dating back to 1918?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we visited three areas, the area of the commander, the area where there was confrontation and fighting, and the area where the camp of detainees was located. I do not remember whether there were other areas that we visited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you recall what you had written in your article, this first position, you saw a gun which had been taken from the museum in Jablanica and was adapted to some sort of defensive combat, defensive fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There you talked to the fighters and their commander whose name is Esad, you took photographs of the command tent and of another gun, 130 millimetres, whom the combatants called their pride. You also found out that this was a gun which was treated very carefully because it was supposed to be shifted to the Sarajevo area to help the fighters trying to break the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were told at the time that that was the only cannon of that type which could be found in the immediate vicinity of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A section of the article where you describe the conditions and the objectives of the fighting with the commander Esad actually reflects what commander Esad had told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your article, he informed you in more detail about the objectives of the struggle, about the frontline and about the fact that there were around 3,000 fighters in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All that he said at the time is what I put down in the article, but I do not remember now exactly all the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you are not quite sure of something regarding my questions, please be so kind as to refresh your memory by consulting your article from July 25th. In fact, commander Esad, according to what you wrote, emphasised that the enemy were at an advantage because they have a heavy long range artillery; is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that place you saw the commandant and the inscriptions written by the fighters on the surrounding trees, the tent and in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, the area where the commander was is different from the area where I saw live shooting between the two parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked to Mr. Hadzihuseinovic, he also proposed this meeting of yours with commander Esad. If I can assist you to remember, it was Esad Ramic, commander of the headquarters of the Territorial Defence of Konjic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to remember that. Mr. Rusmir Haji, when we saw him in the evening, he promised for us to meet the leadership of the area, either the general commander, or he promised to help us go to some military areas. Perhaps this information is not sufficient for you, but I am sorry, I do not remember anything else clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you set out, you knew that Mr. Zejnil Delalic was also in the zone of war operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also knew, Mr. Harraz, that Mr. Zejnil Delalic had done very much, also including his own means, to equip our units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that. What do you mean, to equip the unit? Equip it militarily?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Delalic also gave his personal funds as a successful businessman in the west to help procure the equipment for the army, medicaments, food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzihuseinovic probably told you that Mr. Delalic was co-ordinated between the military and the civil authorities in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knew, Mr. Harraz, that his task in the combat operation zone was to provide the logistic support for the fighters during these very serious combat operations; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what we were told, that he assisted in bolstering military capacities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, thank you. Mr. Harraz, were you told by Mr. Hadzihuseinovic with whom you talked that in fact Mr. Delalic can give you the most accurate data about the status of the equipment and the weapons which our units had at their disposal, as well as in the respect of the needed logistic support, arterial and technical support which was still lacking and was needed by our Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mission was journalistic and therefore I did not ask about details about the kinds of weapons and how they were brought forth. I did not ask such questions, I did not seek such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, is it correct what you have written in your article that you reached the comment posed of Mr. Esad Ramic that it took you two hours to reach the command post of Esad Ramic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If I may object, the witness has stated he does not remember the name of the person other than it was Esad, so I may ask that Defence counsel take that into account when asking her questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I talk about Asad here, I am talking about Asad, but I did not even put down his last name here. As far as I remember, there was somebody else also called Asad. I was told that if there were three people called Asad in Bosnia and my name was Asad and there were two other people also called Asad -- but I do not really remember the family name and I did not get any sweets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you had gotten that it would have been Halva, according to our custom. From the position which you found the commander Esad, you went further on for over half an hour through a forbidding mountainous area until you came to an area where you met with Mr Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was more than 50 kilometres away from the centre of the city, can I say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember in terms of kilometres. The roads were not there at all and I remember it was rainy, so it is difficult to estimate the distance. Half a hour does not mean 50 kilometres; it was not a highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but it took you two hours, you said, to reach commander Esad from the city and then it took you another half a hour or more, so from the city you were on your way for over two and a half hours; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your article you state that you saw a small tent in that area, a tent and a small table on which there were some names carved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also on the surrounding trees you saw various inscriptions in various languages, in particular in English and Arabic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the only thing in English was "general commander", and that was on the location where the commander Zejnil Din was. There were names that were carved into the wood, but I do not remember what names they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember that NATO Alliance and Pentagon and similar inscriptions were carved there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also see several soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All the soldiers present there were Bosnians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- you mean in the site where the commander was or on the battle front? In the site where the commander was there was a small number of soldiers, certainly Bosnians. I do not know whether there were some Croats among them. In the area there were some Croatian soldiers but on that site in particular there was just a small group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You certainly did not see any foreigners there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talked to all of them aided by an interpreter, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this inscription, the main commander's office, was not written in any other language apart from English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were inscriptions or names, but I do not remember what names there were. What I do remember is there was the title of the commander, that was the only thing in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that title, that same thing was not written also in Bosnian; that was the only inscription and the only inscription was in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think all the names were inscribed in Bosnian and in English there was only the title of the commander, "general commander", that was the only thing in English. That is what I remember after five years passing since that visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came there was no reception procedure or ceremony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This place did not give the impression of some kind of a military command where there are pertaining services, equipment, guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was really in the middle of nowhere, it was just somewhere high up with a tent or two and a small group of soldiers who were guarding or assisting the commander, and as I said in the article, close by there was a Bosnian family, and that family took care of catering and helping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic introduced himself to you only stating his name and surname, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was introduced to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He did not say anything about his then or previously held functions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was introduced to us, that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your presence, he gave no orders nor did anyone record to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked with him about the general problems and the political situation in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was interested the most in the procurement of equipment and armaments in view of the fact that our units were poorly equipped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in fact dissatisfied with the assistance being extended by the Arabic world?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position that you had visited prior to that position, there had been many more soldiers, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that position, you were also intercepted by guards.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot remember such minute details. We were escorted by a number of guards who took us to Mr. Zejnil Din.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were where Mr. Delalic was, you could see Serb positions right across from that place and you were warned that their artillery was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were also informed that the combat had been going on for almost three weeks then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned, Mr. Harraz, Mr. Delalic stayed there with these several soldiers of his in the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we left him there and we went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Konjic, you visited a house that you were told was Mr. Delalic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also told that in the basement of that house was the centre of communications of the army of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not exactly. What we were told and what I do remember is that this house was the centre of -- as a meeting point of many people who were responsible in that area for certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have said, Mr. Harraz, on that occasion the spouse of Mr. Delalic, his wife, was presented to you, introduced to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are certain that it was the spouse of Mr. Zejnil Delalic that you met then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot be sure of that. I was told that this was his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This fact, as well as some other facts that you were told, is something that you did not verify or check for yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, and I do repeat that this is what I wrote in the article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, I should now like to ask you several questions associated with your article of July 26th 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we might have the break. We will come back at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. (1.00 pm) (Adjourned until 2.30 pm) (2.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind the witness he is on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I remind you you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, you are still cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Mr. Harraz, may we continue? Before passing on to the most recent article that you wrote, I should just like to ask you regarding your visit to Mr. Delalic's house. You stated in court that there were a lot of people moving about there and that people were meeting there; or rather that that was what you are told; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can confirm, since you saw the house, that the house is next to the road and in a position that is quite sheltered from shelling; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About it being on the road or it being by shelter, I do not know. What I do remember is that there were several people there in front of the house and we were told that that was his main house and that that person we were introduced to was his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you surely know or at least you must have been told that Zejnil Delalic was not in that house for some time because he was on the front and that people were meeting there even when he was not there; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was not present. We left him there at the front and we went to his house, but he was not present in his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to pass on to the article, another article that you said you wrote upon your return from the area, and I would first like to ask you whether you have the original of that article.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean what I wrote with my own hand?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, what was published in the newspaper, an article beginning with your visit to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not quite sure whether I still have this third article or whether I only have a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If it would help Defence counsel, I believe she may wish to look at this since I think this is what she is looking for.

utterances.speaker: MISS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask the usher's assistance to be kind enough to give this article to the witness. I would also like to inform your Honours that this article, or rather photocopies of that article were given to the Defence by the Prosecution, together with a translation into English, so after the original copies have been marked, which will be shown to the witness, that copies of the translation of this article be given to your Honours. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D58/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, this article bearing the date 26th July 1992, when a statement was taken from you in March this year, Ms. Sabine Manke did not ask you about this article, and today, the Prosecution did not ask you any questions about that article; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember anybody asking me anything about this article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Harraz, that you wrote this article as well under the name Assa'ad Taha, as you have already explained; that is bearing the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Assa'ad Taha, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that after visiting Konjic, you headed towards Mostar, and that you wrote this story as well more or less at the same time after your visit to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I remember is that I came back to Split first and then from Split I went to Mostar. I repeat, this is what I remember but I am not sure of it, but what I am certain of is that when we left Mr Zejnil Din, we went to Split.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Harraz, if you look at this article to refresh your memory, is it true that in this article, too, you referred to your visit to Konjic and the conversations you had in Konjic about the situation in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you give me some time to read it again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Would you be kind enough to read it? I will wait. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of the article I refer to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you have refreshed your memory regarding the contents of your article, allow me to address to you a few questions, and if necessary for you to answer those questions, will you please look at the text? Will you please tell me, is it true that you wrote there that the leadership of the Croatian Democratic Union had, a few days before your visit, proclaimed the independence of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not a few days before our arrival, but it is known at the beginning of the war the Croatians declared the union of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, is it true that in this article you wrote that upon your return from Konjic you had to pass through ten or so checkpoints on the main road leading from Konjic to Mostar which was manned by HVO members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to say that in a journalistic omission or in press coverage, it is not always important to specify what city was visited in the beginning or in the end; however it is important for the journalist to stick to the facts. What I said in this article is true, there were many checkpoints on the road to Mostar that were controlled by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that road, you also saw that wherever the control was conducted by the HVO, flags of the Republic of Croatia were flown rather than the flags of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were always there flags of the Croatian Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were one of the few people who had at that time, while there was still an alliance between the HVO and the army, that came to the conclusion that the desire for secession was gaining sway not only over the commanders but over the units of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were expectations that the war would develop into a conflict between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that you learnt from some fighters that HVO members will refused to provide fuel for the TO fighters to enable them to transport the wounded to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was what we were told at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also heard that the HVO had captured trucks transporting humanitarian aid and that this had further aggravated the already difficult situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I repeat, that was what we were told, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you heard and then wrote this down from the mayor of Konjic, Dr. Hadzihuseinovic, that Mate Boban declared the independence of Herceg-Bosna without the knowledge or agreement of the Bosniak side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question or perhaps the interpretation of the question -- perhaps the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that during your visit to Konjic, Mayor Hadzihuseinovic told you, among other things, what you wrote in your article, and I cite: "However, Mate Boban, one of the Croatian leaders in Bosnia, declared the independence of the Croatian republic of Herceg-Bosnia without consulting us." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediately after this quotation you also wrote in this article, so can you please confirm that, that the commander of the units in this region, Esad, had said: "The media of a part of Hercegovina controlled by the HVO and the non-participation of the HVO in defending our areas are creating severe problems for us, especially since those problems are not limited only to their failure to assist, but are also preventing aid from reaching us."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I object because at least in the English translation of this the Defence counsel has misstated the premise. For instance, it does not say that this commander was in charge of the units in this region, so maybe with that clarification I do not object to the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To clear this point up, I should like to ask Mr. Harraz to read this passage in Arabic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Commander Asad said proclaiming Hercegovina independent and the non-participation of Croatian forces in defending our province creates severe problems for us, especially as it does not stop from refraining from extending assistance, but goes beyond that, preventing supplies from reaching us. However, he continued, we cannot deny that we do get some assistance every now and then."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that what Commander Esad told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what Commander Asad told us and I repeat, I do not remember his family name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the Esad you had spoken to earlier on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suppose it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not exactly an objection, but just as a matter of form, I would just either ask if Defence counsel is going to be introducing this in evidence or not, because sometimes it is not clear to me whether or not this witness is testifying from his refreshed recollection or if he is just stating that "it says that in the article" and he now does not have a recollection of it. I do not object either way, but I just note that the record is not clear and it may affect whether or not we have to have this document introduced in some form.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness is answering my questions to the best of his recollection, and I think that in answering questions by the Prosecution, he also said that he had reread the articles, thereby partly refreshing his memory and that is what he is doing now. My questions are linked to the contents described in the mentioned articles which the witness has identified as his own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, what is the object of cross-examining him with the statement which was not referred to in examination-in-chief, unless you have other intentions for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am putting questions to the witness linked to the facts that he has spoken about to certain individuals, his knowledge about those people, the functions they performed and this is just a continuation of the previous testimony of this witness on the basis of two tendered and admitted pieces of evidence. The Defence will probably tender this article as evidence after it has been identified by the witness, because it refers to the same visit and the same circumstances about which this witness is testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are not contradicting him, but you want him to realise that he made such a statement. You want him to appreciate that he made such a statement and then you are reminding him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To confirm what he said, to confirm that this article is his and that he wrote it, and finally, we should like to point to some lack of clarification in his testimony. I would ask to be allowed to complete my questions regarding this article because it all refers to the same subject matter and I think that without this article the picture will not be complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Carry on if you think it is useful.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, Mr. Harraz, we were talking about Esad who, you learnt, had earlier on, as you had written in your article, a captain who used to be a captain in the Yugoslav People's Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, if that is what you wrote in your previous article, then this is a fact that you probably learnt about during your visit; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the information included in the article is based on what we were told then and there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, sir, can you tell me whether at the time you had learnt that this was the person with whom you had discussed various subjects and on various occasions and that in fact he was the commander of the Territorial Defence staff of the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult for me now to remember any details additional to what was included in the article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should just like you to confirm once again something that you have already said. In view of your inability to check the facts regarding certain persons that you met, even after leaving Konjic, and today you are still not absolutely sure which post the various individuals held and what their competence is, or areas of responsibility were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I am certain of is that what was told to me at that time is exactly what I wrote down in my articles.

utterances.speaker: MISS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harraz, I should now like to ask the Trial Chamber, since the totality of the visit is reflected in the three articles written by this witness, and which he has identified here as being his, I would like to tender this article dated 26th July entitled "The Bosnian Croatian union: a marriage out of military interests, divorce because of political contradictions" be admitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Defence counsel is going to do that we would not object but we also ask then that the second article also be admitted into evidence, since it is not clear to me that the second article is admitted. If all three are admitted, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The third article will be D58/1 and the English translation will be D58/1A. I still need to receive the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence will provide a copy of the English translation for the Registry. Thank you, Mr. Harraz. I have finished my cross-examination, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there any other cross-examination? Cross-examined by MR. OLUJIC

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours, with your permission. Good afternoon, Mr. Harraz. I am Defence counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic. Does that name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is hard for me to remember details of names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, you are appearing before the International Tribunal. Do you know who the accused are, what the names of the accused are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know, as I have been told that the first defendant is the Zejnil Din, the commander of the area and the Croatian leader of the camp, but I do not remember his name. I might have written it in my article, but I do not remember it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harraz, before going to Bosnia, how familiar were you with the situation there? How much did you know about it beforehand and did you do any research?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to visit Yugoslavia in general, not just Bosnia, at the beginning of 1990 in general. I did not carry any studies, but the result of various visits, whether to Belgrade or Zagreb or Sarajevo is the knowledge that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, would you be kind enough and tell me whether you went again apart from the times that you describe in these articles when you went to Bosnia? Did you continue to report from the region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not necessarily about that region. I did pass through that region several times to go to Mostar where I went several times, but to Konjic in particular I only passed through, but I did not make any journalistic interviews another time. As for the dates, it is very difficult, because during the three and a half periods of war, I was visiting the area frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, in your examination-in-chief by my learned colleague from the Prosecution, you said that the owner of your newspaper is from Saudi Arabia and that it is published in London; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The newspaper is published in London and it is distributed to the Arab world and Europe and the financial supporter is a Saudi establishment or a Saudi party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is the owner of the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a Saudi person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of journalism is fostered by your newspaper; or rather, what kind of a political orientation does it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a daily political newspaper which deals with general affairs, international affairs as well, in many disciplines, whether political, cultural, economic or otherwise. It had many interests but in general it is a general newspaper. I had stopped collaborating with them for some time now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you permanently employed by them or were you working for them on a freelance basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never worked since my beginning of work as a journalist, as a permanent journalist, I have always worked on a freelance basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harraz, in your testimony, you said that you came to describe events, not to verify facts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I wrote what I have seen and events that I saw at the time and I did not intend to verify the questions that have been raised at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, may it be said that all your articles and all that they contain are based exclusively on your impressions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is based on what I have seen, what I have witnessed with my own eyes, and what I have mentioned -- what has been said to me I have referred to by mentioning the party that said it to me in order to acquit myself of the responsibility. I believe therefore that I did not convey a special impression without some sort of evidence where there is something that I have personally seen or it was said to me, regardless whether that was commensurate with the reality or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mr. Harraz, would you be kind enough to explain for us something you mentioned in your testimony so far. You noticed that the Bosniaks were poorly organised in terms of the chain of command and that sort of thing. Could you clarify this a little?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. At the beginning of the war it was difficult, especially for the Muslim part, because it had no outside party to lend it support. It had to build itself on the administrative side, especially with the lack of experience that they had at the time. What I had touched in that area and then many others is the lack of a hierarchical set-up in the conventional way. This is something that many other foreign correspondents had seen and felt. It was very easy for us to go to any region to visit any person, even if it were combat areas. In other areas it would have been very difficult without going through many steps in order to get the necessary permits to enter these areas. But at the same time I would like to differentiate between the lack of organisation and between chaos. There was no chaos, but I did not see any specific organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, reading your articles, one can see that you spoke to people in the field. Did you have those conversations in the form of interviews by journalists or were they simply -- were your reports simply an interpretation of the conversations that you had with people; in other words when you interview somebody then you have to submit the statement for them to authorise it before it is published in the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The interviews that I had carried out were in the form of questions and answers, and I think I did mention that in the article, that it was a question and answer sort of interview, especially in the camps, in the detention camps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then give those people another chance to read through what would be published in the paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, of course not. There was no time to do that, particularly that when I go back I rewrite the article I have recorded. On that recorder I record the interview, but when I go home I edit it and then I rewrite the article and then I send it to the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Who had organised your visit, Mr. Harraz, when you arrived in Bosnia in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean in Konjic or in Bosnia in general?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am thinking of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, we arrived with a group in the evening, and we met with Mr. Rusmir, we talked together, and he promised us to give us assistance through his relations with others responsible to have interviews the following morning and it was the following morning when we met commander Zejnil Din and where we went to the detention camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had organised this trip, this visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no specific organisation or body that undertakes such an organisation. It was personal initiatives, we had to look for a driver and then a car, that is in Split, then comes the developments that I mentioned earlier. This is the same thing that happened several times and this is the same way that other foreign journalists worked in that area. Every time we have to arrange things probably differ than the previous time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Harraz, you said that you recorded this on a tape recorder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on a cassette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You still have those tapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not have them. I should like to repeat that this is one visit out of many that I have paid to Bosnia during the war years; therefore it is of great difficulty for the journalist to keep all the notes and all the documents that he had, especially that events was not so unique at the time that I had to keep every single shred of paper or evidence of that visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question from my learned colleague, you answered that you saw that Croatian soldiers had the insignia of the republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mentioned that they were carrying Croatian flags. This is what I recall, this is what I remember and what I am sure of, that they were carrying Croatian flags. The identity of these flags, whether it was Bosnia-Herzegovina or Croatia, is difficult for me to ascertain now, but they were carrying Croatian flags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you this precisely to clarify this, because in the transcript it is stated that these were the insignia of the Croatian state.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to ascertain or to deny this fact now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the flag that you saw looks like? Can you describe it to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the colours were red and blue, and there is a certain shape in the middle of the flag that has coloured crossings between red and white, of red and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harraz. I have no further questions. Thank you, your Honours. Cross-examined by MR. MORAN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May it please the court. Good afternoon, sir. My name is Tom Moran and I represent a defendant named Hazim Delic. Does Hazim's name mean anything to you, by the way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a foreign name to me, but I do not remember his position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, that is fair enough. By the way, you testified just a couple of minutes ago that you were told that the first defendant is Zejnil Din. Who told you that? Was it somebody from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I met Mrs. Sabine in London, I enquired about the matter and that is what I understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so someone from the Office of the Prosecutor told you that the person that you interviewed in Bosnia was in fact the defendant in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was said to me is the name, that the name that I had met is now a defendant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so someone from the Office of the Prosecutor said "Zejnil Din equals defendant in this case".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Sir, I think you are a real important witness, and let me tell you why, and then I will tell you what I will do during this cross-examination. You are the first person we have talked to that was in the camp during the period covered by the indictment that is not associated with the war on one side or the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object to this as to relevance. I do not think it is proper for Defence counsel to characterise witnesses in this kind of way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I am doing is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. What I would like to do first is go over your role as a journalist and then go into some specific areas, just about the Konjic area and the camp and then I think we will be done. Sometimes I talk a little fast and sometimes my questions are not as clear as they ought to be. If you do not understand something, will you stop me? I know you speak some English. I know your English is much better than my Arabic. When also you hear through the translator -- I just want to make sure we are communicating when we are talking. As a freelance journalist, basically you work for whoever will hire you on a story-by-story basis. I understand that besides this newspaper that you were writing for when you were in Bosnia in 1992, you have also written for some television channels and in the Arabian Gulf area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as working with the television, with MBC in particular, that was after my visit to the area. It came much later, much later after my visit to Konjic in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also the radio station in Paris was after your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified on your direct examination that you have been travelling almost continually for years. What other types of stories have you covered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They differ as the events differ. Sometimes they are humanitarian, sometimes they are political, and at other times it is military articles but I do concentrate on what I see. I do not pay special attention to something in particular upon which I carry a study. I try to verify the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, did you cover the Persian Gulf War, Operation Desert Storm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not participate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you have covered other wars, other military actions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I covered the Chezcen region and the events of Albania, as well as the events in Zaire Kinshassa, as well as other political events which become hot spots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you have covered humanitarian -- what types of things are we talking about there, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By humanitarian I mean the result of war, the lack and shortage of food, the deterioration of the health situation, the loss of housing and shelter, or any other family problems that might occur. These dramatic events of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, for example, just as sure as I mention this when you were not there, but the starvation in Somalia, that type of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where have you covered these humanitarian missions? Have you seen a lot of starving people while you did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have seen many things as far as humanitarian situations, of great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mainly work for, what, the printed media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I mainly collaborated with the written media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I take it you are more into electronic journalism?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Presently I work with the television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In fact you covered the war in the former Yugoslavia. Almost from the beginning you had a residence visa for Croatia from May 1992 until January of this year, so you must have travelled all over the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but as far as Belgrade, I visited Belgrade at the beginning of the war in May 1992, but after that I was unable to visit Belgrade a second time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was some question about your role as a -- the way you see your role as a journalist. Let me just see if I can explore that for just a second. There are various traditions, of course, in journalism. The tradition that I was brought up under was where a reporter works very hard to be fair and he reports fairly and as accurately as he can what he sees and what he hears and what people tell him. If he has any opinion, it is clearly labelled as opinion. Is that similar to the tradition you were brought up under, the journalistic tradition you were brought up under, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that my article contained that tradition. I have mentioned what I have personally seen, what the people have told me and, of course, it also contained my own impressions and that also came across very clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure, that is what I am saying. It is a very similar unbiased presentation of facts, that is what you are trying to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct, but I should like to say, for example, as far as the camp is concerned, I did not try to seek more information about how were these people detained, were they innocent or were they guilty, such other details and were they really and truly being well-treated or otherwise. Therefore I am saying I did not try to verify these facts because this was not my task, this was not my mission and this needs great assistance, but I only tried to convey reality as I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Another thing I understand, and I think that it may not be as clear as it could be, but just so that it is crystal clear before you and I are done, that when you have written as many stories the last several years as you have, it would not be unusual to totally forget a particular story, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I did not forget what happened, but talking about minute details is something else. I cannot mention such details especially as I fear that what I say could be used for the benefit of this party or that. Perhaps outside this Tribunal I might have my own position, but here I look for the truth and only the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure, and what you wrote down when you wrote those stories in July 1992 was the best set of facts that you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of your biggest -- one of the biggest parts of your assignment for that story or series of stories, as I understand it, was to determine what the conditions were like in the Konjic area; not just the camp but the whole area. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. Our visit to Konjic was not really planned. We had no clear intention to go to Konjic when we left Split. We did not intend to go to such a city and visit such a camp. The point was to go to any area where fighting was going on and where we could get some vision of what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you get a vision or a feel for, for instance, the food supply among the civilians and the military in the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a clear shortage of food among the military and among the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the supply of medicines? Were they plentiful, or could you tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the medical level there was an acute shortage in medicines, and especially in anesthetics and in what makes it possible to do quick surgery in cases of injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me focus on your visit to the camp, and let me start off with that room where they had the large number of people. Based on your experience covering wars, covering humanitarian things, that type of thing, when you looked at those people there did they look like the type of people that you had seen in other places who were starving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As I said repeatedly, the general impression one would have was not that they were subjected to torture or undernourishment, that was the impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That impression you formed was based on a lot of experience, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And having been to places where you had seen people who were starved and tortured and injured, victims of trauma?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not visit areas under Serbian control, so such examples that you are mentioning, I only saw after the release of certain prisoners who had been under Serbian control and went back to Bosnia and told about what they had faced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir, what I am asking you about is whether your impression about the treatment of the prisoners in this camp is based on your personal experience having covered other wars, other humanitarian actions. I do not want to compare it to what occurred in Serbia. I want it based on your experience in other places in the world?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were a lot of signs that would give anybody that impression. I hope you will not be upset, but I will have to repeat again, that was the general impression that one would have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just spent a couple of hours there. I understand what your limitations are on your knowledge. I very much appreciate that. A couple of other things, and then I think we are done. Sir, while you were at the camp -- let me be upfront with you. We have heard some testimony here that several things occurred while you were at the camp. One of the things we heard was that some of the camp guards put on uniforms, I believe the testimony was Serbian uniforms, uniforms with Serbian markings but it may have been Croatian insignia, and then beat the prisoners while this beating was being filmed to make it look like someone else was beating Muslim prisoners. Did you see anything that was even close to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean by beating up Muslims?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The testimony as I recall it was that there was an attempt to have some propaganda or an attempt to show that other people were beating up -- other sides in the war were beating up Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not recall anything of that kind. I do not remember any acts of violence being committed while I was at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if someone were to come and say that people were beaten for a hour in front of you and your cameraman, those people would either be mistaken or they would be lying, would they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, perhaps they are talking about what happened in front of other reporters. I can only say what happened before me in that place and I think even if any torture, beating or humiliations happened, I do not think that would happen before cameras.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there were some testimony that while you and your cameraman were there, people came in disguised to look like they were wounded -- did you see that, any wounded people coming in pretending to be wounded people in front of your cameras?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Serbs, Muslims, I do not care. At the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that camp, as I said previously, as far as I remember there was a small number, three or four, that is what I remember, three or four people who had slight wounds, but I did not see them getting wounded. I just saw them like that and what I understood was they were wounded during battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thinking about wounded, and I think this is the last question; in the infirmary, you said that there were stocks of medicine. How much was there compared with what you have seen in the other parts of the Konjic area about that same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a small table on which there were a few medicines, but what kind of medicine and the quantities -- the room itself was very small and as I said, there were only a few patients, so I think the quantity would be proportionate to the number of patients. I saw a bit of medicine, some cotton, some bandage, but I did not see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Sir, thank you very much. I pass the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any other cross-examination? Is there any re-examination? Re-examined by MS. McHENRY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, a small amount. Sir, in the cross-examination by Ms. Residovic, you talked about how there was a desire among some persons you met and talked with to get additional funding from Arabic countries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said that they were dissatisfied with the little support that they were getting from Arab and Muslim countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic also asked you about the fact that some parts of your article stress Islam and the commitment to Islam amongst some of the persons you talked with; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I said in my conversation with counsel is that I did not find there fundamentalist or extremist Islamic trend, especially as those people had just come out of the communist rule in Yugoslavia. There was not much talk about religion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that although not fundamentalist, there is a reasonable amount of discussion in your articles about Islam and the commitment to Islam, and the desire to have an Islamic state, for instance, in Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think I mentioned in my article the presence of a Muslim state, but perhaps a Muslim presence in view of the number of Muslims in Bosnia. These were individual feelings that were shared with me and that I put down in my article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Ms. Residovic also brought out the fact that, in fact, many Bosnian Muslims were far away from their religion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that you and your editors were conscious of your Arabic readership and wished to have articles that appealed to such an audience, and this may account for some of the stress on Islam in the articles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am an Arab and, of course, those who talk with me know who they are talking to, and perhaps they choose a certain tone or certain words, that is their own choice, but as an Arab they will talk to me as an Arab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that it would not have been appealing nor helpful to those seeking additional funding if the article suggested that prisoners were being tortured or mistreated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are you cross-examining your own witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, not at all. I believe that Ms. Residovic has suggested with her questions that this witness is biased and although it may well be that this witness has some sort of bias, I believe it is important to understand the extent to which there is any and if so, where it comes from so your Honours can evaluate exactly what this witness is and is not saying. I am not cross-examining my own witness at all, your Honour, I am exploring an issue that was raised by the Defence in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, your Honours, I did not put a single such question to the witness, and my witness answered my questions clearly so these questions do not emanate from my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree with Judge Jan, I think she is trying to impeach her own witness. This man has testified he gathered the facts as closely as he could at Celebici and he recounted them to the best of his ability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought she was making a suggestion as to what his own bias was, although it did not arise from cross-examination which is the most important thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I will also make that objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond, let me just point to a couple of questions asked by Defence counsel to which I believe this is directly responsive: "Mr. Harraz, was it one of the intentions of your account of the situation in Konjic to acquaint the Arabic public better with the difficult circumstances in this region and to bolster efforts in providing humanitarian relief?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is nothing to do with bias which you are attributing to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me go forward. The witness answers yes. The next question is: "Mr. Harraz, is that the reason why you perhaps in a certain way placed more stress on the option of these people towards Islam?" I believe those are questions asked in cross-examination and my questions in re-examination are directly related to that issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this question was reworded in the sense of identifying fundamentalism among the Bosnia people and in answer to that question, the witness gave a very precise answer. It is not correct to cite a reworded question as a question that was put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, on a more fundamental note, I am hoping that I have misunderstood the thrust of Ms. McHenry's last statement, but it seems that it is almost as if a person's religion is being used to impeach him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Again, I am hoping I misunderstood what you said, the fact of whatever this man's religion is to whether or not he is a truth teller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: If I may briefly respond, your Honour, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may, but I do not see the need for all this controversy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to state for the record that I do not believe in any way my questions indicated that anything about this person's religion or anyone's religion has an effect on their truth telling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you have any other questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Sir, you also indicated to Ms. Residovic that the soldiers you saw in Konjic were of Bosnian or even Croatian origin, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What soldiers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just the soldiers you met in the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, in the Konjic area there was the commander of the area of the camp who was Croatian and there were also on the battle front some Croats with the Bosnian side, as the soldiers there told me. That is what I also stated in the article.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please just explain to the court what you mean in your articles when you refer to the Mujahedin in the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I meant the Bosnian fighters. I did not meet any Arabs among them or any people from other Muslim countries among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just explain a little bit about what your understanding of --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour, this did not arise out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I believe it did directly arise out of cross-examination and that was, in fact, the reason for Ms. Residovic's question, so I am clarifying any ambiguity that may have arisen from that in connection with the articles -- as I understand correctly, all three have been admitted into evidence, including two of them in cross-examination which contain references and were the focus of Ms. Residovic's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can answer it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you please explain what you understand the common meaning of Mujahedin to be and why it was used in your articles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps the word was used as the article was directly to the Arab public which understands this word which gives a positive connotation to this word, not a negative one, but I do not want to go into this controversial issue. The Mujahedin are people who defend their own lands and do not attack other people's lands, and that is what these people were telling me. They were saying we are defending our lands and will not let our lands be occupied by others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, on a different issue you indicated in response to Mr. Ackerman and possibly also Mr. Moran's questions whether during your visit to the camp you yourself had evidence that the prisoners were mistreated and you said no, you did not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that from what I saw there were no signs of mistreatment. However, what happened after we left or before we arrived, that is something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just then clarify: am I correct that you have indicated that you saw at least some evidence of prisoners being injured before your presence, and you understood from the camp authorities that these injuries had occurred prior to the prisoners arriving to the camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Objection, your Honours, asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That is correct, it has been asked and answered I am just using it as the basis for my question so there would not be any question this was not directly related to cross-examination. Let me then go forward to my ultimate question, sir. Am I correct that your answer to Mr. Ackerman, based that you yourself did not see evidence of mistreatment, was based at least in part on what you had been told by the camp authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not really understand what you mean. I understood the translation itself, but what do you mean by your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He already said, this is what the camp authorities told him. It is already on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. If there is no ambiguity, fine. Sir, let me just again clarify: did you yourself have a video camera or did the video cameraman work for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, there was with me in the area a cameraman that I had met in Croatia and who came with us to the area. As for me, I had a photographic camera with which I took these pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the cameraman did not work for you, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not work for me, he was preparing a documentary and he asked me to write the text, which I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Apart from what you were told, did you see any mistreatment of any of the inmates of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I understand from mistreatment -- if you are asking me whether anybody was mistreated before me, I did not see any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that was all I wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just with respect to a technical matter, it is the case that both the Registrar, as I understand it, the representative from the office of the Registrar and the Prosecutor's office would request that at least the first two original articles from the 24th and 25th, that the original be admitted into evidence since we believe that it is possible that later on there may be some question about the exact quality of pictures. If it is possible after the case is finished they could be returned to the witness, but I would just make that request. I know there was some discussion over it, but the quality of the reproductions is still not as good as the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is 167 and 168?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That is exactly correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is all we have for this witness. You are discharged, you can go. Thank you very much. (The witness withdrew) The Trial Chamber will rise now. We will continue with your next witness when we return. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do we have a copy of the statement which this witness made before the OTP? (Handed) It is not yet part of the record, I just want to look at it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please reswear the witness. BRANKO SUDAR (resworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is time for cross-examination, I think, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to inform you that the Defence counsel for Mr. Delalic has no further questions for this witness. Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: With your permission, your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Proceed, please. Cross-examined by MR. OLUJIC

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Mr. Sudar, let me introduce myself, I am Zejnil Olujic, Defence counsel for Mr. Pavo Mucic, Mr. Zdravko Mucic. You have been here in The Hague for a couple of days now, I shall be very brief, I shall not interrogate you at length, but please, Mr. Sudar, I should like to ask you kindly to be aware of the fact that we speak in a very similar language and understand each other. Lest it seem that we are conducting a dialogue, would you please be so kind as to wait after I have asked my question for the translation into English and, of course, the same goes for the instance when you give me your answer, so that the interpreters will have sufficient time to translate that into the official languages of the court. Mr. Sudar, in your statement, you said that you saw several times Mr. Pavo at the camp. How many times was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Pavo at the camp, he came there, how shall I put it, five or six times at least. We were in the sports hall, but in addition to that, we also loaded and unloaded ammunition, so very frequently we had to go to the hangars to do that. I saw him many times. Sometimes he would come on his bike, sometimes he just stopped in front of the door, would not enter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you also mentioned that you saw a number of uniforms at the camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the camp there were various uniforms, there were a number of uniforms. They would mostly come towards evening, open the door, we would not know who they were or what they were, but there were less Croatian uniforms as far as I could notice. They only came two or three times in black suits. Mostly they were Muslim uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know from your statement, Mr. Sudar, that you are an apolitical person, that you are not all that familiar with politics and that you do not wish to engage in it too much, but what I do want to ask you in connection with these uniforms is whether you were able to identify them. When I say uniforms, were they perhaps police uniforms, predominantly, or soldiers' uniforms? Can you describe them a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were black suits for the most part, we thought they were the black shirts, the HVO, they came two times or three times as far as I could see. After that there were also some people from the Sandzak. They had a Montenegran accent. Mostly these things happened, they were mostly in front of the door, and those who were there could see more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Sudar. Also in your statement you said before this court that the maltreatments inside the camp took place when Mr. Mucic was not at the camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I could notice while I was down there, mostly when Pavo was inside, when he would come inside, they did not hit us, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can one conclude from that that Mr. Mucic protected the prisoners to a certain extent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot decide that, I am not meritorious to say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the -- Mr. Sudar, was any one of the prisoners ever maltreated in the presence of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sudar. Let us clear up a certain point regarding your status. You have refugee status, if I have understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a certain Dr. Bjelica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Bjelica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you have heard of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really, I do not know where this person is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know of the Association of Camp Inmates or Detainees in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, I have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you a member of this Association?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about Dr. Bjelica there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Sudar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: May it please the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Proceed, please. Cross-examined by MR. MORAN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my name is Tom Moran and I represent Hazim Delic here at the Tribunal. I am going to ask you a few questions. Right up front, I know that last week you were not feeling very well. Are you feeling okay today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am feeling better now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. If you experience those chest pains again while we are talking, let me know and we will work with it, okay? No one wants anything bad to happen to you here, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask you a few questions. If you would listen to my questions and just answer them, I think we can get you done here fairly promptly. If a question calls for yes or no, just answer with a yes or no and we can be done here. Can you do that for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you do not understand one of my questions, will you stop me or rephrase it or work with you, whatever it takes so that you understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so there are no surprises here, I am basically going to be asking you questions in the order of your direct examination. There may be a few things that were not covered on direct and I will ask you about those from your statement. The first thing I want to ask you is this. You said that people were buying weapons, Serbians living in the Konjic area and Bradina area were buying weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People were buying weapons because it was obvious to them that the situation was not developing in the desired direction. Some people had weapons, others did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
