utterances.text: What kind of weapons are we talking about? Are we talking about hunting rifles or are we talking about military type weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mostly noticed hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. By the way, you said that there were no Serbian military forces in the area at the time of the attack on your village. When you said that, did you mean there were not any Serbian military forces just in your village or anywhere in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I could see, there were so Serb formations there, how could there have been? We were a village surrounded from all sides. How could there have been any Serb formations there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was not any kind of an organised partisan group or an organised resistance in your village, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in our village, nothing had been organised. People came from Donje Selo, from Bjelasnica; refugees poured in from every quarter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine, sir. Let me jump forward to after the time of your arrest. You were at the bridge, everybody turned over their weapons and were taken into custody; do you remember testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point, you were beaten by the people --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we came to the bridge and all the people were beaten up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to get at, sir, is this: I understand that at that point the people that arrested you, the people that took you into custody took away all your valuables, is that right, that they took all your jewellery and your watches and your rings and your money, anything that was worth anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The watches, everything, driving permit, identity cards, everything, they took everything, even the shoelaces, our belts, everything, my coat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they did that they made you walk about 2.5 kilometres to the camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the camp in the direction of the camp. I cannot tell you exactly how many kilometres, perhaps 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was not a short walk but not a long walk, basically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We crossed the railway line and the bridge towards Celebici and then we followed the railway tracks until we reached the entrance to the camp. I had never been there before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I am going to jump way ahead in your testimony here. You testified on direct about an incident where Mr Delic, you said, fired a shot into the roof of hangar number 6. Do you remember testifying about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He shot the ceiling of hangar number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it what, ricocheted around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it hit the iron structure and ricocheted and hit one of the Kuljanins, I am not quite sure who exactly it was of all the people that were sitting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not saying, are you, that he deliberately shot someone, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that he deliberately shot at someone, he shot at the roof and the bullet ricocheted from the iron structure and hit the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Also on your direct, you testified about a man named Boric. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Boric, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he gave some food to a man named Cecez. What was the first name of that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He gave him food, he brought food to Cedo Cecez, the mechanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether that person is any relation to Grozdana Cecez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether they are related. I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is just one other thing, I think, and then we are going to be done, sir. I do not believe you testified about this on direct, but let me -- do you remember back in August 1992 when the first group of people were released from the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember that Hazim Delic came into hangar number 6 with a list of names of people to be released, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He called out all those names of people to be released, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your name was on that list, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He called my name, yes. I did not dare go home because I heard that before Zivak had left the camp and been killed, so I was afraid of that. The Red Cross people had come and I thought I would be protected in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you are telling these judges is that you had a chance in 1992 to be released from custody and sent home and rather than being released, you chose to stay in the camp because in your opinion it was safer for you; is that what you are telling the judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wish to tell the judges that I did not dare leave because we heard that Zivak had been killed after he left. As the Red Cross people had come I thought I would be protected by them and I did not dare go on account of this story which I had heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. So you had the opportunity to be released in August 1992 and turned down that opportunity because you felt that the camp was a safer place for you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I thought that because the Red Cross had registered us and as Zivak had been killed, this youth that had left before had been killed, I just did not dare go home because I thought I would be killed in my house, on the road, but as I told you, because the Red Cross was there and we had been registered in their cards, I asked to be exchanged -- I did not dare to go home because I thought I would be in the same situation as in the camp and I had no right to go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Pass the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. McMurray. Cross-examined by MS. McMURREY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sudar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I wish you a good afternoon too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Cynthia McMurray and I am one of the attorneys that represents Esad Landzo. I know that the Prosecution, Mr. Niemann, had discussed with you before you testified that you were only to give evidence to this court about things you have personally experienced and personally witnessed. Am I correct about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I have never been in court before. This is the first time, so what do I know? I do not know the court rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the Prosecution discussed with you that you should only give evidence about what you personally know about, is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How can they say anything? I am testifying about what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is all I am asking you. I am asking you, before we begin today, if you and I can come to an agreement that you will listen to my questions and you will only answer about things that you personally saw, personally felt or personally heard. Do we have an agreement on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we have agreed on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Havala. On February 26th 1996, you visited with the Prosecution and after that the Prosecutor let you now that we of the Defence would like to have a chance to visit with you; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that, cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you already stated that you are a member of the association of detainees from Belgrade; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You list as your address the Association of Detainees in Belgrade, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides the Prosecution and your statement that you gave in 1996, what other people have you discussed your experiences at Celebici with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not with anyone. I made this statement and no other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and Mirko Babic are good friends, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you back to your testimony last Thursday. I believe that you said that, and please forgive my pronunciation of these words, I am really bad at some of these, but I am going to try, that Strahinja Cecez and Slobodan Draganic negotiated the conditions of surrender for Cerici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the conditions on surrender. The people called up the President of the municipality to ask him not to shell the place because there was shelling of Cerici, and people called up the President of the municipality, begging him that this should stop and it stopped, because no one was firing from Cerici, nor was anybody fighting from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether it is considered the conditions of surrender or whether it is considered the cease firing on Cerici, those are the two people you named as chief negotiators; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was no surrender, it was calling up the President. He knew him and he spoke to him and then the shelling stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the two people that you named on Thursday, they are the ones who negotiated the ceasefire on Cerici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not about the ceasefire. There was no fire from the Serbian side. No one was shooting, nor were there military uniforms, nothing, we were all civilians in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me. You said these two people negotiated -- what? Is it the ceasing of the shelling by the Territorial Defence and the HVO on Cerici; is that what was negotiated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if -- by the way, do you know a Miro Golubovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miro? Miro Golubovic? I know him, he lived in town but he was born in Cerici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Miro Golubovic said his father Slavo had organised this ceasing of the shelling of Cerici, he would be wrong; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you, Slavko was there, too, and Mirko Cecez was there too, I just mentioned two people, but I was there too, next to my father's house, but we did not go inside, that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you back, I know Thursday seems a long way removed from now, it is hard for me to remember what was said then also, but you said when you were taken to Celebici camp on May 22nd you were put into a small building known as building number 22, which I believe you pointed out on this model; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, number 22, the building is close to the main gates. Later a hospital was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you said there were about 20 of you that were taken to building number 22 at the same time; would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 of us were brought there, and there were some others already there. Among them I recognised Zivak Danilo and Babic Slobodan. Babic Slobodan was covered in blood and lying on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people already in there were just a few people. There was no way in this building number 22 that there were around 100 people in there at one time, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, there were not 100, but 40 or 50 perhaps, I cannot tell you exactly. We were sitting one on top of the other. At that moment I could not look around, I cannot remember, it was terrible. We were one on top of the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Cerici, Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is inside Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is in Bosnia-Herzegovina, former Bosnia-Herzegovina, the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could have voted if you had chosen to in the referendum on March 1st 1992, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What, March 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: March 1st 1992 there was a referendum. I do not know whether you voted or not, but you could have, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I cannot remember these things. I cannot remember that. Whether I voted or not -- I do not know, I think -- I do not know. I have forgotten all those details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was not whether you had voted, it was you had the opportunity and you fit all the criteria to vote if you had chosen to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what to say to that, judges. I do not know what I was supposed to vote for. The people had been divided up at that time. Nobody wanted without Yugoslavia, we did not wish to vote because we were in Yugoslavia and I did not know what to vote for. I cannot really recall the exact point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when you arrived on May 22nd 1992 at Celebici, it is true that the Celebici camp was mainly run by HVO officers then, HVO soldiers, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that. How could I have said that, it was mainly run by the HVO. There were military men, Muslims, I do not know. I noticed there were a few wearing black shirts, black suits. We were forced to line up against the wall, we could not see. We had to hold our hands up like this against the wall (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were absent from the Celebici camp from what dates, from May 22nd until what date was it that you arrived at the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until Bajram, the holiday, Bajram. I cannot remember the date, but I know it was Bajram when I was transferred back from the sports hall to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that myself I am not familiar with the Islamic faith and I do not know whether at least two of the judges are, but for clarification, can you give us a date somewhere near when Bajram begins?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It was June as far as I can recall, as far as I know, but it was a long time ago. I cannot recall, but I do remember that it was Bajram that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say June, I think your testimony before was that you spent about 20 days at Musala; is that pretty accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, I did not count the days. I was under pressure, how could I count? As if any of us could count. Nobody counted, nor did I have time to count. Roughly, I do not know exactly the number of days, I just do remember that it was Bajram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back to Celebici --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delic brought me back and there were another two or three or four, I do not know, I cannot remember. Someone else was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Sudar, remember we talked about having an agreement earlier. I would just like you to listen to my question. I did not ask you who brought you back. I am asking you about the date you were brought back and I am trying to get the dates accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume, since I do not know when Bajram is, that you returned to Celebici some time in the middle of June, would that be close?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell exactly. All I know is that it was Bajram. I did not know what date it was, out of fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a date in the middle of June when about seven or eight new young guards were brought to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some time in the middle of June, around June 12th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember those details. Maybe if I can think back a little, but I cannot remember the day. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking if you remember an incident when a number of young guards, 18 or 19 year old guards were brought to Celebici some time around the middle of June. If you do not remember, that is fine too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe when you came back to Celebici, you were placed in hangar number 6; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified on Thursday that you sat close to the doorway facing it with your back; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was sitting in the second row near the entrance, third or fourth, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask the assistance of the usher, please? This is a picture that has already been marked in Prosecution exhibit number 1, they have been kind enough to give me a clean piece of it. I would like to have it shown to the witness and placed on the ELMO, please. I would also like to have it marked as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is marked as D17/4.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. (Handed). Can we have it turned on and ask the witness to look at it please? I know there is a pointer there but does he have a pencil or pen that he can mark on this exhibit with? Mr. Sudar, if you will look at the actual drawing that is on the ELMO, thank you. Do you recognise that as hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the door was here somewhere (indicates). The main gate was over there and the road was there. There was a concrete part and the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask you to describe it for me. Do you recognise that as what looks like the inside of hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot, it was in steel. How can I recognise it? It was a steel structure. I am not good with drawings. I am no draftsman. It was a hangar made of steel. I did not measure it in steps length wise or width wise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many months you spent in hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in hangar number 6 from Bajram until the beginning of September, something like that. I cannot recall the dates. The dates are the most difficult for me to remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look back at the exhibit that is on the ELMO. Do you recognise that the door in the lower right hand column would be what would represent the door that opened in hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, the approach?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like for you to look at it and see if -- this is an exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recognise drawings, only if I was to see the hangar properly made. I am not very good with drawings, I do not understand them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I was going to ask you to do is put an X on the spot approximately where you sat inside of the hangar, but if you cannot recognise the hangar at all, then I will not be able to ask you that question. Can you recognise the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object, your Honour. The witness has said repeatedly that he does not recognise the drawing of the hangar. On that basis, I object to further questions being put to this witness on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess if he does not recognise that as hangar number 6 then I certainly cannot proceed with any further questions on that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought as much.

utterances.speaker: MISS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That is correct. Could I ask the usher's assistance one more time, please? I would like the record to reflect that the witness was unable to identify hangar number 6 as introduced by the Prosecution. Could this be marked as another Defence exhibit and placed on the ELMO also.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I object to that characterisation. The witness was not shown hangar number 6, the witness was shown an exhibit. So I would ask that the record reflect that the witness was not able to identify the hangar from the exhibit that was shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might respond, I just wanted the record to reflect that the witness did not recognise a Prosecution exhibit that has been introduced into evidence. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us get the sequence of the questions. The witness was shown an exhibit representing the hangar. He was unable to identify it, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, that clears it up completely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can recognise the rows, but not the hangar. I cannot recognise the drawing, but I can show you the rows of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Maybe you will have a little more success with this next exhibit. Could we exchange the first exhibit with the second exhibit, please? Mr. Sudar, I know that this is not completely proportionate, this is just an estimation of how it might have appeared and I know there were people sitting on another side of the building there that are not reflected in this drawing, but can you look at this exhibit and can you recognise it as something that might be close to the seating arrangement that was inside hangar number 6 in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In hangar number 6, like this, there was a row going along here, round here, all the way round. Then there was a row like this and another row like this. I was in this row. I do not know exactly -- there was some people behind me, I suppose. Somewhere here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for clarification, the wall to the right had a row of people seated along it also, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not a wall, it is sheet metal. I do not know that there was any wall. It was metal, steel, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, but you do recognise this as close to the seating arrangement of the detainees inside hangar number 6; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do I know about the seating arrangement? There were more than 50 people in one row. The door was here somewhere and here there was no one, there was a bucket for toilet purposes here and we would eat here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is; do you recognise this as something familiar to you, familiar, almost like the seating arrangement was in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is something like this, it looks like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand drawings well, but if I were to see a building, a model, then maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: the place that is marked on there that says -- I do not have it in front of me, but looks like it is approximately where you were seated, can you tell us how many people were seated to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my right? Again, I do not know exactly. There were 250 of us, I did not count. There was a wall to the right on both sides, the people were sitting on both sides of the hangar in several rows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look back at this drawing again. You see two of the rows, the rows closest to the door are facing toward the back wall of the hangar and the two rows on the back wall of the hangar are facing toward the door; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two rows were facing forward and the other two were facing towards the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were facing with your back to the door; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I would turn around now and then. I turned around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were put in hangar number 6, I believe you also testified the other day "we mostly had to sit with our hands on our knees, crouching, and we had to bend our heads down in that position." Was that not your testimony on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is how we sat but in the meantime when they would pass by, we would turn around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you did lift your head up when a guard was inside the hangar, you would get punished, would you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would pass by us, they would go down to the end of the building, they would lead a dog. I could look up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you one more time before I leave your exhibit and I am sorry, Mr Registrar, did I get a document number for that one?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: On that one, if you look approximately at where you were seated, facing the back wall of the hangar, how many people were closer to the door than you were in the row you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the names of those people, there were people were all over, from Bjelasnica, from Sarajevo, from Bradina, from Sarajevo. There was Babic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking their names, I just want to know how many. I do not want to know who they are, just how many were seated closer to the door to your right approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my right -- when I came I was the last, then afterwards two or three were brought in later, Amici, somebody called Zivak, Zivak Amici, I cannot remember those men, three or four of them, I suppose, sometimes five, it depends when they were brought in, thrown in. How do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony is that some time during that period of time you could have been fourth, fifth or sixth in that row?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the details exactly. I said that when I first came I was at the end, then afterwards three or four men were brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like for you to look again at this drawing. The door that is there in the corner of hangar number 6, the hinge of that door is on the corner of the building and it opens outward, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, I cannot recognise drawings. This is more slanting than it was, I think, in my opinion. If I were to see the hangar and enter the hangar then, of course, I would feel differently and I would get my way around more easily. I do not understand drawings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were facing the hangar from the outside and the door is to the right, over to the right outside the hangar was a hill, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a slope, when you went to the toilet, there was a hill behind the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this drawing, can you also show us where Nedeljko Draganic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nedeljko Draganic sat in the third row facing me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that toward the back of the hangar or toward the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the middle row, but further away from me, up there, somewhere near the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the end to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I cannot remember these details. I did not count.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point with your pointer on the diagram approximately where you think Nedeljko Draganic sat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly he was sitting here somewhere in this row. How many people there were I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You need to point on the drawing behind you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was this row, he was here somewhere, I think, but I cannot recall exactly. Here, this part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to let the record reflect, it reflects row 3, about two-thirds back to the back of the hangar, where he has pointed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Further up, further here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe that is about three, four down towards the back of the hangar. Would you also show us where (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted), he was near him. I do not know exactly, but he was there somewhere. We would change around sometimes so I do not know. He would make him get up and then he would change his position, so I do not know all the details, I cannot recall them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were never moved to another position in hangar number 6 for the whole time you were there, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in my place all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I would like to have this admitted as Defence exhibit number 18/4 to illustrate where this person approximately sat in the hangar and what his view was of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we object to the tender of this exhibit. It has not been identified by this witness, the witness has consistently said that he cannot recognise drawings. The way it was put to him is "do you recognise it as something familiar to you, almost like the seating arrangements" in my submission your Honours we would be much assisted by having the person who drew the plan come before the court and tell us what factors he took into account and upon what basis he determined measurements and so forth. I think if that evidence is given to the court, there would be no objection to it based on what this witness has said. My suggestion, your Honours, is that it be marked for identification and when the author of the plan comes forward to give us that necessary information, it can be tendered at that stage, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond? I believe that Mr. Niemann's attempt to prevent this document from coming into evidence is his approach to that -- whoever made this is irrelevant. If the Defence made it as a Defence exhibit and the witness recognises it as nearly or close to representing the seating arrangement in 1992, then it should be admitted for demonstrative purposes. We are asking that the court recognise that this witness has said that was where he was sitting, he identified where Nedeljko Draganic was sitting, he identified where (redacted), and it also shows where the door was and how he was facing. I think it is very helpful and instructive for this court to be able to have it before it when it is considering all the evidence at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is part of your evidence, the site plan. All she is asking the witness is to identify the place where he was sitting. This is part of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I do not believe it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is a copy of that, I think. This is a photograph. What she is interested in finding out from the site plan, from the one she showed to him first, is where he was sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has said that he does not recognise drawings. He specifically stated that the angle of the view is not correct; he believes it is too slanted. When pressed, and I did not object to the continuing questioning of this witness when he was protesting about his inability to recognise drawings and that if he had been shown the hangar or presumably a model of it he would have been happy with that, but he continually expressed his dissatisfaction on being questioned on that, I did not object to that and I am not objecting ultimately to the tender of this document, all I am saying is there is insufficient information which has been given to the court on the accuracy of the document for in any way it to be reliable. All it requires is for whoever drew it to come forward and give us the basis on which it was drawn, and then I am sure that would put the document into a category of accuracy and reliability which would make it admissible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might respond briefly? This document is not introduced for the accuracy of building number 6. It is introduced only to identify approximately where this witness was seated during the whole time he stayed in hangar number 6. He testified he never moved. He testified that this did look familiar to him. He said these were the witnesses, they were seated this way, there were about 50 on each row, and he was able to identify his location in the hangar, and we are offering it only for that purpose. Who drew it is irrelevant. It is only that the witness can identify it and he can point out where he was located on this drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, the Trial Chamber has building number 6 as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do you not have enough material to identify the place he was sitting? He was in the second row, facing towards the back, away from the door. That should be sufficient for your purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The description is sufficient for whatever you want to use it for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was in the second row, facing towards the other side. That should be sufficient for you.

utterances.speaker: MISS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Of course, for demonstrative purposes, I would prefer to have the Chamber be able to refer to this document at a later time. I would ask that it be admitted, as I do think the record is clear, but I would like to ask that this document be admitted for demonstrative purposes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Because of the nature of the answers the witness is giving, it does not appear he is sufficiently conversant with what that particular exhibit is demonstrating. It might be fairly difficult, except we rely on a description of where he was sitting and imagine whether he could see all parts of the plan from that point. I thought in fact in the first stage you could have used building number 6, which is already an exhibit, for the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would have loved to have used that, that would have been more instructive, I would have put it in with all the other prosecution exhibits showing the same location, but this witness said he did not recognise it, so I had to go to another venue to try to get the information in. I will withdraw that exhibit right now, but I would like to show the witness another drawing at this time and see if he can recognise this. I will save that for another witness who can identify it. Thank you. Could I have the assistance of the usher again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you show me the model I will say whatever is necessary, but I do not find my way around drawings. One would have to draw the people on these drawings, it would be necessary to draw each individual head of each individual detainee, and I just cannot find my way around on drawings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it from this model possible to remove the roof so he can show us?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, for his protection he is not able to walk in front of the model right now, and it inhibits us, unless we go into closed session, and then I do not know that we would have a camera to look down to show the court and preserve it for your review at a later time either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has identified the place where the hangar was, and if the roof was removed he could probably indicate the place he was sitting, but all the curtains have to come down so he can walk up. If it is important for you we can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that if you are satisfied that you understand where he was seated -- he was facing a different direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I am quite clear for myself. He sat second row, facing towards the other side from the door, and he was sitting nearer the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: About four, five or six people in. Then that is clear, I will leave that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There is too much tendency here for arguing matters which are clearly understood. I do not see the point at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I withdraw that, but I would like to have this exhibit marked as D19/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is another exhibit I would like to place before the witness. Mr. Sudar, can you look at this drawing? Is this approximately how you were asked to sit, what position you were forced to sit in in hangar number 6, not only you but all the other detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not sit like this. Like this (indicates) that is how we sat, and on this drawing you have depicted us with our heads completely bowed down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I really do not understand what you are about. Do you think people are machines? Merely because they were asked to sit like that, they cannot at any stage, no matter what happens, turn around? He has been telling us all along that whenever they had the opportunity, they turned around. Why are you insisting that he could not do so?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am attempting to impeach him, because if he raises his head he is punished, any time there is a guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I agree. They did not discover him to punish him, but he did it. I think the Trial Chamber will break now. You can continue tomorrow morning. (5.35 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day) 21 22 23 24 25
